title: Create vendored Standard Schema v1 types file
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

Create a new file `lib/types/standard-schema.ts` containing the vendored StandardSchemaV1 interface from the Standard Schema spec (https://standardschema.dev). This is a types-only file — no runtime code. Include the `StandardSchemaV1` interface, `StandardSchemaV1.Result`, `StandardSchemaV1.SuccessResult`, `StandardSchemaV1.FailureResult`, `StandardSchemaV1.Issue`, and `StandardSchemaV1.IssuePath` types. Add a comment at the top referencing the spec URL and version (v1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/lib/src/lib/types/standard-schema.ts` exists
- [ ] Contains the full `StandardSchemaV1` interface with nested types (Issue, Result, SuccessResult, FailureResult, IssuePath)
- [ ] Has a doc comment referencing https://standardschema.dev and https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema
- [ ] Types are exported
- [ ] TypeScript compiles with no errors (`npm run build`)

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: Add validation logic in dispatchRequest after transformResponse
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

In `dispatchRequest.ts`, after `transformResponse` is applied to `response.data` in the SUCCESS path, add inline schema validation logic. If `config.responseSchema` is defined:
1. `await config.responseSchema['~standard'].validate(response.data)`
2. If result has `issues`: create a `FaxiosError` with message `'Response validation failed'`, code `FaxiosError.ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA`, pass config/request/response, set `error.issues = result.issues`, throw it.
3. If result has `value`: set `response.data = result.value`

Add a `// ponytail: extract to helper if request schema (#15) repeats this pattern` comment.

IMPORTANT: This logic must ONLY run in the success path (where `validateStatus` passed), NOT in the rejection/error handler path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `responseSchema` is set and validation passes, `response.data` is replaced with `result.value`
- [ ] When `responseSchema` is set and validation fails, throws `FaxiosError` with code `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA` and `issues` property
- [ ] The thrown error has `response` attached (with original data)
- [ ] Validation is `await`ed (supports async schemas)
- [ ] When `responseSchema` is not set, behavior is unchanged (passthrough)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles with no errors

## Blocked by

- schema-2
- schema-3

title: Skip schema validation on HTTP error path
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

Ensure the schema validation logic added in schema-4 does NOT run in the rejection handler of `dispatchRequest.ts`. The rejection handler (where `validateStatus` returned false) also applies `transformResponse` — but schema validation must be skipped there because error response bodies don't match success schemas.

Verify this is already the case from schema-4's placement (it should be — validation was added only to the success path). If so, this task is just adding the test that proves it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a request returns a status that `validateStatus` rejects (e.g. 404), the response schema `~standard.validate` is NOT called
- [ ] The error thrown is `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE` (the HTTP status error), not `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA`
- [ ] Unit test verifies this behavior

## Blocked by

- schema-4

title: Add isSchemaValidationError type guard to FaxiosError
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

Add a type guard function `isSchemaValidationError` in `lib/core/FaxiosError.ts`. The function:
1. Takes `unknown` as input
2. Returns `err is FaxiosError & { issues: StandardSchemaV1Issue[] }`
3. Checks: `isFaxiosError(err) && err.code === FaxiosError.ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA && Array.isArray(err.issues)`

Import `StandardSchemaV1Issue` type from the vendored types (or reference the nested type from `StandardSchemaV1`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isSchemaValidationError` function exists in `FaxiosError.ts`
- [ ] Returns true for FaxiosError with code `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA` and issues array
- [ ] Returns false for other FaxiosErrors, non-FaxiosErrors, and non-errors
- [ ] TypeScript narrows the type correctly when used in an `if` block
- [ ] TypeScript compiles with no errors

title: Add conditional type inference for responseSchema output
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

Update the TypeScript generics on request methods (`.get()`, `.post()`, etc.) and the `FaxiosResponse` type so that when `responseSchema: StandardSchemaV1<any, O>` is present in the config, `response.data` resolves to `O` instead of the default `unknown` or manual `<T>` generic.

This likely requires:
- A utility type that extracts the output type from a `StandardSchemaV1` (e.g. `type InferSchemaOutput<S> = S extends StandardSchemaV1<any, infer O> ? O : unknown`)
- Overloads or conditional types on the Faxios class methods that detect when config contains `responseSchema`

When both a manual generic `<T>` and `responseSchema` are provided, `responseSchema` output type wins (it's the runtime truth).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `faxios.get('/url', { responseSchema: MySchema })` infers `response.data` as schema's output type
- [ ] `faxios.get<ManualType>('/url')` without schema still works (backward compatible)
- [ ] When both manual generic and responseSchema present, schema type wins
- [ ] `faxios.create({ responseSchema })` instance methods infer correctly
- [ ] TypeScript compiles with no errors
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing generic usage

## Blocked by

- schema-2

title: Unit tests: schema validation success, failure, and async
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

Unit tests for the validation logic in `dispatchRequest.ts`. Use mock Standard Schema objects (plain objects implementing the `~standard` interface) — do NOT add zod/valibot as test dependencies.

Mock schema examples:
- Sync success: `{ '~standard': { version: 1, vendor: 'test', validate: (v) => ({ value: v }) } }`
- Sync failure: `{ '~standard': { version: 1, vendor: 'test', validate: () => ({ issues: [{ message: 'bad' }] }) } }`
- Async success: `{ '~standard': { version: 1, vendor: 'test', validate: async (v) => ({ value: v }) } }`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test: valid data → `response.data` replaced with `result.value`
- [ ] Test: invalid data → throws `FaxiosError` with code `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA`
- [ ] Test: thrown error has `issues` array from schema result
- [ ] Test: thrown error has `response` with original data
- [ ] Test: async schema that returns Promise<Result> works
- [ ] Test: no `responseSchema` in config → response unchanged (passthrough)
- [ ] All tests pass

title: Integration test: full lifecycle with instance-level schema
body:
## Parent

#4

## What to build

End-to-end integration test that exercises the full request lifecycle with schema validation. Use a mock HTTP server (from `tests/setup/server.js` pattern) and a mock Standard Schema object.

Test scenarios:
1. Create instance with `responseSchema` via `faxios.create()`
2. Make request, get valid JSON response → `response.data` is the validated/parsed value
3. Make request, get invalid JSON response → caught error is `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE_SCHEMA` with issues
4. Per-request schema overrides instance schema

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test: instance-level `responseSchema` validates all responses from that instance
- [ ] Test: per-request `responseSchema` overrides instance default
- [ ] Test: response interceptors receive the validated (replaced) data
- [ ] All tests pass with `npm run test:vitest:unit`
